footer.tagline: Green coffee from the hill districts of eastern Nepal. First lots arriving after July 2026.
footer.disclaimer: Cup scores and lot details on this site are reported by producers and have not yet been independently verified. We are arranging UK cupping. Nothing here is a commercial offer until samples have been scored in Britain.

hero.alt: Cloud moving across a forested ridge in the hill districts of eastern Nepal, a dirt road cut into the slope

premise.title: Our Story
premise.body1: Nepal is better known for its mountains than its coffee. But among the hills below the Himalayas, coffee has been flourishing for decades.Grown at elevations between roughly 800 and 1,600 metres, Nepalese coffee benefits from cool temperatures, distinct seasons and abundant monsoon rainfall. These conditions allow the cherries to develop slowly, building the foundations for complex and expressive coffees.Across Nepal’s coffee-growing regions, differences in altitude, climate and landscape create distinct flavours and character.
premise.body2: This is coffee shaped by Nepal’s unique landscape: carefully cultivated and unmistakably of its place.

journey.title: We went to the hills and asked
journey.body1: Reaching a producer in eastern Nepal takes a flight, a bus, and then a road that is mostly suggestion. Landslides close it in the monsoon. The last stretch is walked.
journey.body2: We made that trip — through Gulmi, Bhojpur, Ilam and Solukhumbu — to see the trees, taste what comes off them, and sit with the people who tend them. Not a sourcing trip arranged by an exporter. We turned up, and we kept turning up.
journey.pullquote: You cannot judge a coffee from a spreadsheet. You have to stand in the row and look at the tree.
journey.captionRoad: The public bus is often the only way up. In monsoon, landslides can close the road for days.
journey.altRoad: A brightly painted bus on a narrow hillside road, dwarfed by dense green forest in eastern Nepal
journey.altValley: Two forested ridges converging into a deep valley, cloud gathering in the gap

growers.title: Farms of a hectare, sometimes less
growers.body1: Most of the coffee here is grown by families, on plots measured in hundreds of trees rather than hectares. Coffee sits alongside cardamom, citrus and whatever else the slope will hold. It is one income among several, which makes what a buyer pays matter enormously.
growers.body2: We deal with the cooperatives and producers directly. We know which washing station handled which lot, whose trees it came from, and what altitude it grew at. When something is uncertain, we say so.
growers.altFarmhouse: A tin-roofed farmhouse in the Nepali hills with dahlias flowering in the foreground and cloud descending the mountainside behind

coffee.title: What is actually in the bag
coffee.body1: Predominantly Arabica, with some Robusta at lower altitude in parts of Koshi. Washed, natural and yellow honey processing, depending on the producer and what the weather allowed that season.
coffee.body2: Producer-reported cup scores currently sit in the 81–85 band, with moisture below 11%. Those are their numbers, not ours — and we treat them as a starting point rather than a claim.
coffee.altCherry: A single ripe red coffee cherry on the branch, surrounded by wet green leaves after rain

map.title: Four districts, two provinces
map.body: Gulmi and the Lumbini hills to the west; Bhojpur, Ilam and Solukhumbu in Koshi to the east. Different altitudes, different processing traditions, genuinely different cups.
map.alt: Map of Nepal showing Mewa Valley Coffee's sourcing districts across Koshi and Lumbini provinces

verify.title: Nothing is confirmed until it is cupped in Britain
verify.body1: Every figure on this site came from a producer. We have not yet put these lots in front of an independent UK cupping table, and until we do, we are not going to tell you they are specialty grade.
verify.body2: Samples are being arranged now. When they are scored, we will publish what comes back — including the lots that do not make the cut.
verify.pointOneBody: Named cooperative, district and altitude for every lot.
verify.pointTwoBody: Producer figures are marked as producer figures.
verify.pointThreeBody: UK cupping results go up whatever they say.

cta.title: Come and taste it before anyone else has
cta.body: We are looking for a small number of UK and European roasters to evaluate the first samples. If Nepal sounds like a gap in your offering, we would like to hear from you.

about.title: About us
about.aboutBody1: The coffee we source grows in the foothills of the Himalaya. Nepal's climate suits it: cool dry winters, warm monsoon summers, and reliable rain at the point in the year the cherry needs it most.
about.aboutBody2: There is a young, fast-moving coffee culture in Nepal that Europe knows nothing about. We want to bring that community — and what it grows — to Britain.
about.sourcingBody1: We are in active conversation with several producers at different stages of readiness, from established exporters to farms shipping their first commercial lots. They span the hill districts of Koshi and Lumbini: Gulmi, Bhojpur, Ilam and Solukhumbu.
about.hillAlt: Hills near Mewa Valley Coffee's sourcing districts in Nepal
about.mapAlt: Map of Mewa Valley Coffee's sourcing districts in Nepal
about.sourcingBody2: Between them our producers work across washed, natural and yellow honey processing. Predominantly Arabica, with some Robusta at lower altitude in parts of Koshi Province.
about.sourcingBody3: Growing altitudes run from roughly 800 to 1,600 metres. Higher up, the cherry ripens slowly — sugars concentrate and the bean comes out denser.
about.sourcingBody4: We are looking to work with roasters who find that as interesting as we do.
